strings: A sign that shows there are doors here. There are doors everywhere!
A huge chunk of reinforced metal used to separate rooms.
A huge chunk of iron used to separate rooms.
A window that is reinforced with metal rods.
A little bit of nature contained in a pot.
A one meter section of regular pipe.
Damn, they better have the /tg/ channel on these things.
A spawner for cockroaches, the most common vermin in the station. Small chance to spawn a bloodroach.
It's a storage unit for emergency breath masks and O2 tanks.
A sign with the Nanotrasen logo on it. Glory to Nanotrasen!
A small screen which the AI can use to present itself.
A flexible, superconducting insulated cable for heavy-duty power transfer.
Has a valve and pump attached to it.
A warning sign which reads 'SECURE AREA'.
A reinforced version of the four legged table.
Some rods. Can be used for building or something.
A wrench with common uses. Can be found in your hand.
This box is shaped on the inside so that only light tubes and bulbs fit.
A small wall mounted cabinet designed to hold a fire extinguisher.
A trusty station intercom, ready to spring into action even when the headsets go silent.
What did I say about leaning on the glass tables? Now you need surgery.
Light and airtight plastic flaps made to keep the cold room cold and the warm room warm.
Four metal legs with four framing rods for a table. You could easily pass through this.
A machine that monitors atmosphere levels. Goes off if the area is dangerous.
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. This one has a glass panel. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
A heavy duty blast door that opens mechanically.
It's a storage unit for tools.
A basin used to grow plants in.
A large piece of space-resistant printed paper.
Displays the status of mechs connected to the recharge station.
Deploy to designate the landing zone of the auxiliary base.
A square piece of iron standing on four metal legs. It can not move.
The label indicates that it contains body bags.
It's a normal black ink pen.
Now you see me, now you don't...
A standard Nanotrasen-licensed newsfeed handler for use in commercial space stations. All the news you absolutely have no use for, in one place!
Perfectly designed to be comfortable to sit on, and hellish to sleep on.
Pull this in case of emergency. Thus, keep pulling it forever.
An industrial computer integrated with a camera-assisted rapid construction drone.
Used to call and send the mining shuttle.
Come on Lady Luck, spawn me a pair of sunglasses.
A canister for the storage of gas.
It has some unsavory stains on it...
For connecting portables devices related to atmospherics control.
A very complex router and transmitter capable of connecting electronic devices together. Looks fragile.
It's a floor-mounted device for projecting holographic images.
Do not apply fire to this. Rumour says it burns easily.
Contains all the paper you'll ever need, in duplicate!
A rubber stamp for stamping important documents.
A console intended to send requests to different departments on the station.
You shouldn't see this. Report it please.
This sheet is an alloy of iron and plasma.
A freezer containing packs of blood.
An arcade machine is guaranteed to spawn here. The normal atlas view shows one possible cabinet from the source pool; the actual game is chosen when the round starts.
Contains all the paper you'll never need.
For the exotic art of paper shuffling.
Soft velvet carpeting. Feels good between your toes.
Contains condensed capsaicin for use in law \"enforcement.\"
A wall-mounted first aid station, designed to treat minor injuries - just stick your hand in and try to relax.
You sit in this. Either by will or force.
A board for pinning important notices upon. It is made of the finest Spanish cork.
A heavily reinforced case containing cyborg logic boards, with space for a standard power cell.
The Warrior's bland acronym, MMI, obscures the true horror of this monstrosity, that nevertheless has become standard-issue on Nanotrasen stations.
It's black and greasy. Looks like Beepsky made another mess.
It's slippery and gooey. Perhaps it's the chef's cooking?
Different from the Middle Ages version.
A lightbulb you can walk on without breaking it, amazing.
A catwalk for easier EVA maneuvering and cable placement.
A transit tube for moving things around.
A technological marvel, supposedly able to mix just the mixture you'd like to drink the moment you ask for one.
black and red space suit replica
A plastic replica of the Syndicate space suit. You'll look just like a real murderous Syndicate agent in this! This is a toy, it is not made for use in space!
A plastic replica of a Syndicate agent's space helmet. You'll look just like a real murderous Syndicate agent in this! This is a toy, it is not made for use in space!
A double sided angled mirror for reflecting laser beams.
All engineering related spawners go here
A heads-up display that scans the humanoids in view and provides accurate data about their health status.
One bug squashed. Four more will rise in its place.
It says \"Sternside Changs #1 fan\" on it.
A cheap, plastic replica of an energy sword. Realistic sounds! Ages 8 and up.
Used to copy important documents and anatomy studies.
It's green and acidic. It looks like... blood?
It's a storage unit for fire-fighting supplies.
A thin layer of dust coating the floor.
A lightweight support lattice. These hold our station together.
Used to modify prisoner IDs, as well as manage security implants placed inside convicts and parolees.
A brave janitor cyborg gave its life to produce such an amazing combination of speed and utility.
Used to access the various cameras on the station.
A control terminal for the area's electrical systems.
Used to view and edit personnel's security records.
This port recharges a mech's internal power cell.
A simple vending machine suitable to dispense well tailored science clothing. Endorsed by Space Cubans.
Basic railing meant to protect idiots like you from falling.
A tactical security uniform for officers, complete with a Lopland belt buckle.
Use this to keep prisoners in line.
This is used to lie in, sleep in or strap on.
A poster instructing the viewer to walk instead of running.
A big book used to store photos and mementos.
Downloads personal AI assistants to accompany its owner or others.
A soft and fluffy pillow. You can smack someone with this!

A standard issue Security gas mask with integrated 'Compli-o-nator 3000' device. Plays over a dozen pre-recorded compliance phrases designed to get scumbags to stand still whilst you tase them. Do not tamper with the device.
A robust flashlight used by security.
A rainbow blanket with a clown mask woven in. It smells faintly of bananas.
A poster encouraging the swift reporting of crime or seditious behavior to station security.
It's a secure locker for personnel. The first person to swipe their ID gains control.
All the class of a trenchcoat without the security fibers.
A really cool hat if you're a mobster. A really lame hat if you're not.
Some type of shrubbery. Known for causing considerable economic stress on designers.
You can't tell if this is real grass or just cheap plastic imitation.
A bluespace teleporter used for teleporting prisoners to the labor camp.
An old, deactivated cyborg. Whilst once actively used to guard against intruders, it now simply intimidates them with its cold, steely gaze.
A sink used for washing one's hands and face. Passively reclaims water over time.
A covered turret that shoots at its enemies.
A desk lamp with an adjustable mount.
A one meter junction that connects regular and heat-exchanging pipe.
A secure crate containing various materials for building a customised test-site.
HOLY SHEET! That is a lot of glass.

A plastic pressure bag, or 'chem pack', for IV administration of drugs. It is fitted with a thermosealing strip.

A highly precise directional sensor array which measures the release of quants from decaying tachyons. The doppler shifting of the mirror-image formed by these quants can reveal the size, location and temporal affects of energetic disturbances within a large radius ahead of the array.
A computer designed to handle the calculations and routing required for sending and receiving mechs from orbit. Requires a link to a nearby Orbital Mech Pad to function.

A massive module rack which can hold many modules including a core law module. 		It can even be linked to other module racks to add additional slots. 		Designed to be used by the station's primary AI and its legion of cyborgs.
A holographic projector that creates holographic engineering barriers. You can remotely open barriers with it.
Goes great with a glass of warm milk.
A container designed to hold compressed matter awaiting reconstruction.
A box containing a compactly packed machine. Use multitool to deploy.
A link to the netverse. It has an assortment of cables to connect yourself to a virtual domain.
Flooring that shows its contents underneath. Engineers love it!
A Chinese classic, it's Donk's original spicy orange chicken with stir-fried peppers and onions, all over steamed rice.
Donk Co's signature Donkhiladas with Donk sauce, for an 'authentic' taste of Mexico.
A TV dinner classic: \"crispy\" fried chicken in country gravy, mashed potatoes, and green beans.
A small contraption designed to imbue a few drinks with a pleasant chill.
Works just as well as a metal one.
A display case for prized possessions.
A sign labelling a saferoom where the station's resources and self-destruct are secured.
It's still good. Four second rule!
An intercom that broadcasts any ongoing interrogation to someone that's probably taking notes.
A console with access to the mining, auxiliary base and vault camera networks.
A vending machine rumoured to be capable of dispensing clothing for medical personnel.

A custom-built grappling-hook powered by a winch capable of hauling the user. 		While some older models of cargo-oriented grapples have capacities of a few tons, 		these are only capable of working in zero-gravity environments, a blessing to some Engineers.
A stationary computer. This one comes preloaded with research programs.
A terahertz-ray emitter and scanner used to detect underfloor objects such as cables and pipes.
A self cleaning vending machine capable of dispensing clothing for janitors.
Protects your hearing from loud noises, and quiet ones as well.
A medical spray bottle. This one contains hercuri, a medicine used to negate the effects of dangerous high-temperature environments. Careful not to freeze the patient!
Basic burn ointment, rated effective for second degree burns with proper bandaging, though it's still an effective stabilizer for worse burns. Not terribly good at outright healing burns though.
An ordinary cardboard box with holes cut in the sides.
A helmet made out of a box.
A compressed fuel pellet for long-distance drone flight.
Used to call and send the labor camp shuttle.
It is decorated with a key emblem. For those rare moments when you can rest and cuddle with Ian without someone screaming for you over the radio.
The latest set of collectable action figures.
WEEEEOOO. WEEEEEOOO. STOP THAT MONKEY. WEEEOOOO.
Place this as the corner of your 3x3 multiblock fusion reactor
Activate this with a multitool to deploy the full machine after setting up the other boxes
A skeletal limb wrapped in pseudomuscles, with a low-conductivity case.
A telescreen with access to the research division's camera network.
It produces items using iron, glass, plastic and maybe some more.
A figurine depicting a reptillian Geneticist donning a labcoat, staring at you with evil intent.
A headset that is a result of the mating between medical and science.
A long list of rules to be followed when in the library, extolling the virtues of being quiet at all times and threatening those who would dare eat hot food inside.
Box of stuff used to implant chemicals.
Box full of scum-bag tracking utensils.
A comfy-looking cat bed. You can even strap your pet in, in case the gravity turns off.
A telescreen that connects to the engine's camera network.
Used to grind things up into raw materials and liquids.
A formal relic of years past before Nanotrasen decided it was cheaper to dye the suits red instead of washing out the blood.
An underfloor disposal pipe which sorts wrapped and unwrapped objects.
A luxurious double bed, for those too important for small dreams.
A heretical poster depicting the titular star of an equally heretical book.
A standard issue colored jumpsuit. Variety is the spice of life!
It's a baseball hat in a tasteless white colour.
A sterile mask designed to help prevent the spread of diseases.
Monitors the details of the telecommunications network it's synced with.
A pneumatic waste disposal unit. This one leads to the morgue.
This machine has a dish-like shape and green lights. It is designed to detect and process subspace radio activity.
A volcanic rock. Pioneers used to ride these babies for miles.
A telescreen that connects to the minisat's camera network.
A robust satchel for stashing your loot.
Used to view crew member accounts and purchases.
Traditional burial garments from the early 22nd century.
A figurine depicting a Medical Doctor, donning a labcoat & syringe.

A rapid and safe way to stabilize patients in critical condition for personnel without advanced medical knowledge. Contains a powerful preservative that can delay decomposition when applied to a dead body, and stop the production of histamine during an allergic reaction.
An expertly modified RCD outfitted to construct plumbing machinery.
Helps with burn injuries. Does minor eye damage. Diluted with Granibitaluri.
A hefty machine that, when supplied with iron and glass, will periodically create a drone shell. Does not need to be manually operated.
Accept boulders and refines metallic ores into sheets.
The janitorial department's trusty pet lizard.
A glass lab container for storing interesting creatures.
This is my BROOMSTICK! It can be used manually or braced with two hands to sweep items as you move. It has a telescopic handle for compact storage.
An insult to Duke Purple is an insult to the Space Queen! Any proper gentleman will fight you, if you sully this tea.
A mighty piece of hardware used to send/receive massive amounts of data.
A vending machine for dispensing chemistry related clothing.
For the enterprising botanist on the go. Less efficient than the stationary model, it creates one seed per plant.
It is decorated with a shield emblem. While crime doesn't sleep, you do, but you are still THE LAW!
A specialized medical kit for when the ordnance lab -spontaneously- burns down.
Dispenses countless types of pipes. Very useful if you need pipes.
Rubber ducky you're so fine, you make bathtime lots of fuuun. Rubber ducky I'm awfully fooooond of yooooouuuu~
AURUMILL-Brand Baby's First Training Toolbox. A digital display on the back keeps track of hits made by the user. Second toolbox sold separately!
An ailing, old, repurposed cargo hauler. Most of its equipment wires are frayed or missing and its frame is rusted.
A novelty coin that helps the heart know what hard evidence cannot prove.
A small, easily concealable toy handgun. Ages 8 and up.
The spawner of the keg on the station. Special stuff on Beer Day and St. Patrick's Day.
Your favorite brand, now menthol flavored.
Control exploration drones from interstellar distances. Communication lag not included.
IT'S A STORAGE UNIT FOR FIGHTER MASKS OLE!
A plastic sign backing, use a pen to change the decal. It can be placed on a wall.
A huge metal vat with a tap on the front. Filled with cooking oil for use in frying food.
A machine used for recycling dead monkeys into monkey cubes.
For the hard-working tradesperson who's in the middle of nowhere and just wants to warm up their pastry-based savoury item from an overpriced vending machine.
A figurine depicting the standard outfit of a captain belonging to a civilian-sector Nanotrasen station.
A poster instructing the viewer to report suspicious activity to the security force.
A refrigerated storage unit for slime extracts.
A warning sign which reads 'HIGH EXPLOSIVES'.
A gold flask belonging to the captain.
Nanotrasen has issued posters, like this one, to all stations reminding them that rumours of a gas giant are false.
A figurine depicting the glorious head of the Security department.
A locked box used to store medals of honor.
A console for assigning civilian bounties to inserted ID cards, and for controlling the bounty pad for export.
A poster glorifying the station's security force.
A die with twenty sides. The preferred die to throw at the GM.
This poster is lookin' pretty trippy man.
It's milk. White and nutritious goodness!
It's soy milk. White and nutritious goodness!
NexaCache(tm)! Dubiously authentic gear for the digital daredevil.
A spring loaded gun designed to fit syringes, used to incapacitate unruly patients from a distance.
A machine for dispensing clothing related to genetics.
Autonomous Power Loader Unit Subtype Paddy. A Modified MK-I Ripley design intended for light security use.
Used to send criminals to the Labor Camp.
Used for watching the AI and the RD's goons from the safety of his office.

A device installed in order to control moisture in poorly ventilated areas. The stagnant water inside basin seems to produce serious biofouling issues when improperly maintained. This unit in particular seems to be teeming with life! Who thought mother Gaia could assert herself so vigorously in this sterile and desolate place?
A figurine depicting the glorious head of the Science department.
Enlist in the Nanotrasen Deathsquadron reserves today!
An altar which allows the head of the church to choose a sect of religious teachings as well as provide sacrifices to earn favor.
A specially-reinforced camera with a long lasting battery, used to monitor the bomb testing site. An external light is attached to the top.
A vending machine designed to dispense clothing and tools for roboticists.
There is a small label that reads \"For Emergency use only\" along with details for safe use of the tool. As if.
box of shotgun shells (Less Lethal - Rubber Shot)
A box full of rubber shot shotgun shells, designed for shotguns.
A figurine depicting a Bartender looking stylish with their rockin shades and tophat.
It's Officer Pingsky! Delegated to satellite guard duty for harbouring anti-human sentiment.
This is a space piano, like a regular piano, but always in tune! Even if the musician isn't.
Wearing these makes you look useless, and only good for your sex appeal.
Fancy dress for space bar singers.
It appears to have a beaker emblem, and is made out of fire-resistant material, although it probably won't protect you in the event of fires you're familiar with every day.
Cargo's pet sloth. She's dressed in a horrible sweater.
A sign labelling an area where scientific data is stored.
A figurine depicting that silent bastard you are all too familiar with.
A figurine depicting someone in a black and green modsuit, nobody has any clue to what this is.
A machine used to deposit and withdraw station funds.
Used to monitor the crew's PDA messages, as well as request console messages.
A large crushing machine used to recycle small items inefficiently. There are lights on the side.
A light-weight titanium wall used in shuttles.
An engine that releases a large bluespace burst to propel it.
A comfortable, secure seat. It has a more sturdy looking buckling system, for smoother flights.
A wall mounted safe containing space suits. Will only open in emergencies.
